why: Every operation adds or subtracts one power of two, so this is about n's binary form: an isolated 1-bit costs one subtraction, while a run of 1-bits is cheaper to round up (one addition turns the run into a single carry bit). The week pairs it with DP, but the greedy over bits is the whole solution (a DP over bits with a carry state gives the same answer).
hints: Write 6 = 110 and 21 = 10101 in binary. Count the answers against the 1-bits.
Scan from the lowest bit. A single 1 followed by 0 should be subtracted; a 1 followed by another 1 (bits ...11) should be removed by adding 1, which carries the run into one higher bit.
Loop while n > 0: if n is odd, count one op and do n += 1 when n & 3 == 3, else n -= 1; then shift right. O(log n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Counting the 1-bits (popcount) is wrong for runs: 7 = 111 needs 2 ops (8 - 1), not 3.
The pair 0b11 at the very top (n = 3) still rounds up: 3 -> 4 -> 0 is 2 ops, same as 2 + 1, so either choice is fine there.
n is up to 2^40: fine in Python, but use a 64-bit type in other languages.
